newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Troubled Ansett set for Air NZ, Singapore alliance.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Ansett set for Air NZ, Singapore alliance.

text.p: Airline Ansett Australia, struggling to overcome losses from its fledgling Asian regional carrier, is set to announce an alliance with Air New Zealand and Singapore Airlines on Friday.

Ansett said on Thursday Ansett International expected a loss of A$50 million (US$37.5 million) in the 1996/97 year ending June 30 and that it was due to hold a joint news conference on Friday morning with Air New Zealand Ltd and Singapore Airlines.
It would not say what would be announced, but it is widely expected that Singapore Airlines would become an equal partner with News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd in Ansett Australia.
Currently News and Air New Zealand own Ansett 50/50.

Ansett's regional carrier, Ansett International, is owned 49 percent by News and 51 percent by local institutions and has struggled to make profits since its launch three years ago of flights to seven Asian destinations.
"That's (A$50 million loss) Ansett International's stand alone result," Ansett International general manager Craig Wallace told a tourism conference in Melbourne.
Wallace said that the international operations' loss would be offset by operating income from Ansett's domestic and other business .
"The loss is significantly reduced from there."
"The consolidated Ansett group is talking about break-even," he said.

Wallace said the break-even result followed a similar performance in 1995/96 and represented the foundation for the Ansett group's goal of driving profitability to acceptable levels within three years.
Meanwhile Ansett reiterated it was committed to selling non-core assets, but declined to comment on a report it was about sell its 68.2 percent stake in Diners Club Australia.
A Sydney Morning Herald report said Ansett was set to sell its Diners Club for up to A$43 million to a local or foreign bank.
Also, Ansett and Air New Zealand's main competitor Qantas Airways Ltd said it continued to look at ways of getting into the New Zealand market.

"We've explored a number of possibilities in New Zealand, ranging from being in the market in our own right, to a possible partnership, but no decisions have been taken," Qantas managing director James Strong told Reuters.
